text: ABSTRACT
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > ABSTRACT

text: A defect free copper interconnect is crucial for ensuring the electrical connection and transmission of high density interconnect printed circuit boards. Leveling agent is a key regulatory factor for achieving dense cop per super filling from bottom to top in blind holes during the electroplating process of high-density interconnect boards. Here, two small molecule five-membered heterocyclic compounds with different side chains, namely 3- amino-5-mercapto-1,2,4-triazole (AMT) and 2–5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazole (MMT), were selected to be as levelling agents to study their effect on the copper filling behavior on blind holes. Electrochemical tests including cyclic voltammetry solvation (CV) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) were firstly used to analyze the inhibitory effect of two leveling agents on copper deposition and it was indicated that the MMT has a more significant inhibitory effect on the copper deposition than the AMT.
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > ABSTRACT

text: Subsequently, the influence of different concentrations of MMT on the inhibition of copper deposition and the blind hole filling performance were also further analyzed by LSV, CV, and constant current measurement (GM), where an optimal concentration of 7 ppm was obtained for the maximum inhibitory ability on the copper deposition accompanied by the best blind hole filling ability. The characterization analysis from the field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) also illuminates that the MMT leveling agent can effectively reduce the surface roughness of copper filled with micropores and promote the selective growth of copper coatings along the (11 1) crystallographic plane. The adsorption behavior of the levelling agent on the cathode surface during electrodeposition was further also studied by the quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics sim ulations combined with the in situ electrochemical surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) experiments.
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > ABSTRACT

text: It has been suggested that the thiol, sulfur, and alkyl groups in the leveling agent MMT molecule are nucleophilic groups, providing preferred active sites for adsorption reactions and thus generating effective inhibition ability on copper deposition formation. Thermal shock experiments based on tin immersion showed the copper layer obtained under the addition of the levelling agent MMT has excellent reliability. The comprehensive results indicated that 2-mercapto-5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazole (MMT) was an effective levelling agent for the blind hole supperfilling.

text: 1. Introduction
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 1. Introduction

text: Blind hole copper electroplating is the primary technology used in the connectivity manufacturing process for printed circuit boards (PCB), semiconductor integrated circuit (IC) chips, and IC packaging substrates [1–3]. The issue of achieving complete filling of high-quality plated copper has become increasingly essential in light of the progress made in integrated and miniaturized electronic devices. This is particularly relevant as high-density interconnect printed circuit boards (PCBs) are transitioning towards through-hole and micro-hole designs with larger depth-to-diameter ratios [4]. In the process of copper plating on such PCB micro vias with a larger depth-to-diameter ratio, there is a very significant difference between a current’s density distribution inside and on the surface of the micro vias. In such an environment, the copper electrodeposition rate in the pore area will be significantly greater than that in the micropores’ bottom region, which will result in the coppe layer covering and sealing the pore area in a preferential manner, leading to internal defects in the pores.

text: In order to achieve bottom-up superfilling of the micropores, a synergistic effect of different addi tives is required, namely accelerators, inhibitors, levelling agents and chloride ions. Accelerators are generally small molecule organic sul phides containing specific functional groups of (-S–S-), sulfhydryl (-SH) and sulphonic acid ( - S O _ 3 ^ -) groups, which typically preferentially adsorb at the micropore’s bottom and can hasten the electrodeposition of copper at the hole’s bottom. SPS and MPS are both common accelerator [ 5, 6 ]. During copper electrodeposition, the inhibitor is usually adsorbed on the cathode surface and interacts with chloride ions to increase the overpotential, thereby achieving the inhibitory effect on the surface deposition of copper, Inhibitors are mainly macromolecular polyether or polyols [7]. The most prevalent inhibitors are polyethylene glycol (PEG), but in addition to PEG there are also polypropylene glycol (PPG) and triblock copolymers of PEG and PPG [8–10]. Levelling agents can be added in very small amounts compared to inhibitors to achieve a strong inhibiting effect and rapid deactivation, leaving the surface flat and smooth.

text: Meantime, levelling agents also show an inhibiting effect o copper deposition but there is no substitute for inhibitors, which can be compared to short-acting inhibitors, while inhibitors show a moderate inhibiting effect and deactivate slowly, and throughout the plating process, the levelling agent gradually covers the copper surface, domi nating the completion of superconformal deposition [4,7]. Traditiona levelling agents such as Janus Green B (JGB), Diazine Black (DB) Methylene Blue (MB), Alsin Blue (ABPV) [11–14]. However, these dye conventional levelling agents are prone to decomposition at high tem peratures, which makes the plating process not easy to control increasing the cost and also leading to copper plating quality problems. In response to the above problems, researchers have continued t develop new environmentally friendly high-performance small molecul copper plating levelling agents, such as benzyl quaternary ammonium containing compounds phenylacetyl chloride (BZC) [15], 2,2-dithiodi pyridine (DTDP) [16], 4,6-dimethyl-2-mercaptopyrimidine (DMP) [17], tricyclazole (TCA) [18], 1-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-tetrazole-5-thion (HPTT) [19].

The threeelectrode test system employed had a platinum rotating disc electrode (Pt-RDE) with a 5 mm diameter as the working electrode (WE), a saturated calomel electrode as the reference electrode (RE) and a platinum wire electrode as the counter electrode (CE). Here, the base solution was 220 g / LCuSO _4·5H_2O (technical grade), 55 g/L H 2 SO 4 (98 %, analytical reagent, AR) and 60 ppm Cl - (37 % HCl, AR), the accelerator used in this study was Bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS), the inhibitor was polyethylene glycol (PEG), and the levelling agent was two small molecule five-membered heterocyclic compounds, namely AMT (99 %+, Adamas, Shanghai) and MMT (98 %, Adamas, Shanghai). The concentration of accelerator SPS was 0.1 g / L, the concentration of inhibitor PEG was 1 0 : g/L,, and Both the levelling agent (AMT、MMT) had a 0.1 g/ L concentration.

text: 2.2. Electrodeposition
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 2.2. Electrodeposition

text: There are two types of PCBs, each with a different size blind hole (the hole size and depth were 120 μm x75 μm and 100 μm x 125 μm, respectively) were employed in the blind hole electroplating filling experiment. Before electroplating, the copper plate containing 0.0 4 % ~ 0.065 % phosphorus is wrapped in a filter bag as the anode, and the surface oxide of the copper plate containing phosphorus is polished off with 1000 mesh and 2000 mesh sandpaper before use. After rinsed off the sanding with deionized water, the surface oxide is activated with 1 mol/L sulfuric acid for 3 min, and the surface oxide is completely removed. Ensure that the anode plate can fully react during the plating process, and rinse the residual sulfuric acid with deionized water after removal. Before use, the filter bag is activated in 1 mol/L sulfuric acid for 3 min, and then washed with deionized water. Finally, the treated phosphorus-containing copper plate is placed into the treated filter bag and placed into the electrolytic cell. The cathode PCB board should be etched in an acidic solution for 5 min. Then rinse it off with deionized water.

text: Quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations were performed using the Visualizer, Forcete and Dmol modules of the Material Studio (MS) software. For the simulations, the force field is selected from COMPASS, DFT generic functional theory, and the density distributions of the highest occupied molecular orbitals (HOMO), lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (density distributions of the highest occupied molecular orbitals (LUMO) and the energy gaps ( Δ E = E_LUMO - E_HOMO), and the electrostatic potentials (ESP) are calculated.

section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 3. Results and discussion

text: 3.1. Electrochemical properties of two leveling agents are compared
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 3.1. Electrochemical properties of two leveling agents are compared

text: First, using cyclic voltammetric stripping, which was carried out in a base solution with SPS and PEG, SPS, PEG, and MMT/AMT, respectively, at two rotational speeds of 100 rpm and 1600 rpm, the effect of two types of five-membered heterocyclic compounds with different side chains on the electrodeposition behavior of copper was investigated. The findings are depicted in Fig. 2. The observation of Fig. 2 reveals that the dissolution peaks of copper obtained from electroplating solutions containing two kinds of small molecule five membered heterocyclic compounds additives are significantly smaller than those obtained from the base plating solution whether at the 100 rpm or at the 1600 rpm. The results of the aforementioned inquiry suggest that the introduction of two small molecules consisting of five-membered heterocyclic compounds can effectively enhance cathodic polarization and prevent the deposition of copper. Moreover, it was further observed that the copper dissolution peak was smaller when 5 ppm MMT was added than when 5 ppm AMT was added. This means that the additive MMT is superior to AMT in inhibiting copper deposition through levelling agents.
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 3.1. Electrochemical properties of two leveling agents are compared

text: The effects of the two levelling agents on copper electrodeposition were explored further using linear scanning voltammetry (LSV), and the findings are displayed in Fig. 3. From this, we can see when 5 ppm AMT and 5 ppm MMT are added whether in weak or strong convection, Copper’s deposition potential significantly shifts towards the negative direction, which is consistent with the results obtained from CV, indicating that the addition of AMT and MMT both can inhibit copper electrodeposition. Moreover, Copper’s deposition potential attained in the plating solution containing MMT shifts to the negative direction to the greatest extent, indicating that the additive MMT has a greater ability to suppress copper deposition compared to the additive AMT.

text: 3.2. Electrochemical analysis of the additive MMT
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 3.2. Electrochemical analysis of the additive MMT

text: Based on the above results that the MMT levelling agent exhibits a greater inhibitory ability to copper deposition compared with the AMT, Further research has been done to investigate how MMT levelling agent interacts with other additives. Initially, a constant current test was conducted at a rotational speed of 1600 rpm to investigate the effects of different concentrations of MMT additives on the inhibitory properties of copper deposition. As depicted in Fig. 4 displays the curves represent the relationship between potential and time. From Fig. 4, 200 ppm inhibitor PEG was added at 200 s, 1 ppm accelerator SPS was added at 500 s, and 1 ppm levelling agent MMT was first added at 1000 s. When 1 ppm MMT was added, the deposition potential was negatively shifted at 1000 s and the cathodic polarization was increased, which indicated that MMT inhibited the deposition of copper. The deposition potentials at a total of 7 ppm MMT and 9 ppm MMT were essentially the same, so the optimum concentration of levelling agent MMT was tentatively concluded to be 7 ppm.

text: Furthermore, the objective of this research is to examine the impact of various concentrations of MMT additive on the inhibition of copper deposition behavior by the utilization of cyclic voltammetric solvation analysis. The findings are presented in Fig. 5. As depicted in Fig. ^5, at 1600 rpm, the copper dissolving peak displayed a trend toward decreasing behavior as the levelling agent MMT concentration was raised from zero to 7 ppm. The copper dissolving peak did not further diminish when the MMT additive concentration was raised to 9 ppm; rather, it essentially remained the same as the copper dissolution peak attained at 7 ppm. Therefore, it can be determined that the optimal concentration of the leveling agent MMT with the strongest copper inhibition ability is 7 ppm, which is consistent with the results obtained from the constant flow rate experiment.

As shown in the figure, the peak of copper dissolution under strong convection (i.e., at 1600 rpm) conditions is significantly smaller than that under weak convection conditions (i.e., at 100 rpm). E LUMO closely related to the molecule’s ability to accept electrons and E_HOMO to the molecule’s correlates with the ability to give electrons [16]. ΔE represents the adsorption strength of the molecule at the copper interface, the smaller ΔE indicates that the additive molecule is more stable and has a stronger adsorption capacity on the surface. text: 4. Conclusion
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 4. Conclusion

text: In summary, two small five-membered heterocyclic compounds with different side chains, namely AMT and MMT, were selected as electroplated copper levelling agents in this paper. The electrochemical anal ysis of CV, LSV, and GM showed that MMT has greater inhibitory ability in inhibiting copper deposition behavior compared to AMT. An optima concentration (7 ppm) of MMT added for effectively suppressing copper deposition was obtained by electrochemical analysis from the CV, LSV, and GM experiments based on the addition of different concentrations of MMT additives. The blind hole filling experiment further demonstrates that such an optimal addition concentration for MMT can achieve cop per overfilling in high aspect ratio PCB blind holes. Characterization analyses from FE-SEM, AFM, and XRD also further demonstrate that the coating obtained at this optimal concentration of MMT has the densest and smoothest surface with a typical 111 texture preferential growth. The thermal shock experiment based on tin immersion indicates that the copper layer obtained using MMT as a leveling agent has good reli ability.
section: Five-membered heterocyclic small molecule compounds as novel levelling agents for blind-hole copper plating > 4. Conclusion

text: It is indicated by in-situ Raman spectroscopy analysis that the adsorption of MMT molecules on the electrode surface is a time dependent process and the C–S, C–N, N––N, and - CH bonds are preferentially adsorbed on the electrode surface. The smaller energy gap value (ΔE = 3.729 (ev)) for the MMT molecule calculated by quantum chemistry further indicates that suggest that the MMT molecules have strong adsorption capacity. Furthermore, Quantum chemical calcula tions based on the electronic potential energy of the MMT molecula structure indicate that the thiol group, sulfur bond, and alkyl groups from the MMT molecular belong to nucleophilic groups and provides the preferred adsorption reaction active sites for interaction with the copper surface, which is consistent with the results from the in situ electrochemical enhanced Raman spectroscopy. The adsorption of these nucleophilic groups on the copper surface effectively inhibits copper deposition and thereby achieving bottom-up copper overfilling in blind holes. These results from the electrochemical analysis and theoretical calculations fully demonstrate that MMT is an effective levelling agent for PCB blind hole filling.
